lines.context: She has one end of a crate of empty bottles off the ground. The other end is still on the pavement. She looks at it. Then at you.
She sets her end down, takes your hand, and puts it on the handle at the far end of the crate. Then she lifts her own end again, and waits.

lines.text: Wat? Nee, ick will keen Jeld!

lines.context: She taps the handle of the crate twice, then her own chest, then yours. Two people. One crate.
She taps a word stamped on the side of the crates you have just stacked, and looks at you with her eyebrows up.
She waits, arms folded. The word on the crate has not got any easier to read.
She puts one hand flat on her own chest.
She unfolds a chair by the window with one shake, points at it, and then at you.

lines.text: Ooch jut. Der Stuhl looft nich weg.

lines.context: She points at the hotel next door, lays her cheek on her folded hands like a pillow, and then points at the pavement where you are standing.

lines.text: Nee! Morgen. Nich jetzt. Erst schlafen, denn wiederkommen.

lines.context: She holds out a paper cup with steam coming off it, tilted towards you.
The young woman in the hoodie looks at you, then at Kerstin, and changes language without being asked.
lines.text: Oh - you're the new guy? She told me about you. Want me to translate?
Okay. She says she's been standing here since ninety-eight, and that you look like you need breakfast.
Gotta run, lecture. Good luck with her!

lines.context: She taps the doorframe of the shop, then flicks up her fingers: nine, then eight.
lines.text: Icke steh hier seit achtundneunzig, wa.
Englisch? Nee. Russisch hatt ick inner Schule.

lines.context: She draws a line in the air with one finger, straight across the road, and then looks at it for a moment.
lines.text: Und da drüben war die Mauer. Weeßte?

lines.context: She nods at you, then up at the sky, and back at you, as if she has a guess and is not going to say it.

lines.text: Sie? Wir sind hier nich beim Amt.

lines.context: She waves the Sie away like a fly.
She looks down the street towards the U-Bahn, the way you look for a bus that is late. Then at a second chair, folded against the window - not yours. She counts on her fingers, up to seven.
lines.text: Emil kommt nich mehr. Seit ner Woche.

lines.context: She comes out with a paper bag - bread rolls, a folded newspaper - and holds it out to you. She points north, walks two fingers across her palm, and says a place. Twice.
lines.text: Bring ma die Tüte zu Emil. Kollwitzplatz. Kollwitzplatz. Der sitzt da imma.

lines.context: An old man on the bench by the playground, one leg stretched straight out in front of him. He looks at the bag in your hands, then at you, and does not smile.
lines.text: Wat soll dit? Ick kenn Se nich.
Ick brauch keen Almosen, junger Mann.

lines.context: He has not taken the bag. He is waiting for a better reason than pity.

lines.text: Hallo! Junger Mann! Wat is dit?

lines.context: He taps his knee, then points across the square at the U-Bahn entrance, and makes a face at the stairs going down.
lines.text: Dit Knie. Die Treppen am Senefelderplatz. Deswegen komm ick nich.

lines.context: He holds up six fingers, then taps the last square in a row printed on the back of his newspaper. Then he points at you, and back the way you came.
lines.text: Sagen Se Kerstin: Samstag komm ick. Knie hin oder her.

lines.context: He holds out his hand. Not for anything. To shake.
lines.text: Ick bin Emil. Wir können uns ruhig duzen.

lines.context: She is watching the corner where the U-Bahn comes up. She looks at your empty hands - the bag has gone - and then at your face.

lines.text: Denn hol ick ihn ab. Samstag.
Hat er se jenommen? Die Tüte?
Samstag is Wiesn. Erst schlafen, wa.

lines.context: Kerstin is wearing a dress with a laced bodice and a white apron, and she is standing in it the way you stand in the rain.
lines.text: Guck nich so. Dit is'n Dirndl. Von meener Schwester aus München.
Hör uff. Ick seh aus wie ne Kuckucksuhr.
Jenau. Ick seh aus wie ne Kuckucksuhr.
Ick seh aus wie ne Kuckucksuhr, ick weeß.

lines.context: She taps a calendar taped inside the shop door - today's square has a ring drawn round it - then points at you, then at the U-Bahn.
lines.text: Heute is Samstag. Wiesn. Kommste mit?
Dit is nich unsa. Dit is Bayern. Aber jut.

lines.context: Kerstin looks at Emil's knee, then at your chair by the window, then at you.
lines.text: Emil braucht nen Stuhl. Nimmste den mit?
Dit Knie is nich so schlimm.
Setz dir, Neuer. Is dein Stuhl.

the holiday reel
lines.text: Dit is nich unsa. Dit is Bayern.

lines.context: the holiday reel
Arda turns the tray towards you. One glass is dark red; another is almost gold. His eyebrows rise. There is room for you in the circle.
He sets the tea back and points at a sealed bottle of water. Selin shifts sideways to leave you the same space as before.
Hasan reaches towards the light glass. Selin glances at it. Arda has turned away to collect the empty saucers.
He draws a loaf on a scrap of paper, then a little hook above it. He points towards the Çarşı and waits to see what you make of the drawing.
Arda draws the loaf and the hook again. Then he points towards the lane you came from.
Hasan hands you his phone to photograph some food packages. As you raise it, he steps into the edge of the frame. Selin lowers the phone with one finger and looks at him.
Hasan is happy to take the picture, but shakes his head when you point the phone at him. Selin turns the phone towards the packages, leaving every face outside the frame.
He sets the tray down. His hand rests on it for a moment. He holds up one finger, then rubs his wrist.
Hasan reaches towards the tray. Arda rests a palm beside it and looks at him. You remember the finger, the wrist, the minute.
He writes ARDA under the tray on a small drawing, then holds the pen towards you. His finger moves from you to an empty place on the paper.
They are sorting sweets and food packages for their Bayram visits. Selin marks an empty space beside them on Arda's drawing. She leaves the tray where it is.
Hasan offers his hand. Selin waves from beside the packages. Arda is already smiling. Three greetings, and none of them has waited for a perfect sentence.
He holds up the light and dark glasses, then points to the water. This time he waits for you to name what you want.
lines.text: Açık mı, demli mi? Yoksa su mu?

lines.context: Selin points to one small parcel and the clear spot beside her. Then she points to the gathering. You can help with this one thing, or join as the guest she invited.
Val has brought a box from the caff. A parcel of folded notices sits on the pavement beside her. She nods towards it without putting her box down.
lines.text: You couldn't give me a hand with those, could you?
Lovely. The notices, please. This box is eating my fingers.

lines.context: She tips her head towards the parcel and the clear patch of pavement. Now the request has a thing and a place attached to it.
lines.text: Could you put them beside me?
No worries. Ahmed, could you take the other end?
Not for me. For my niece.

lines.context: Val reaches for milk. Mr Ahmed takes out his phone. There are two empty cups, but his niece is not here to point at either.

lines.text: We share a surname. Not a tea order.
She's replied. No milk. One sugar.

lines.context: She draws a cup on a scrap of paper, crosses out a sugar cube, and adds a tiny pigeon. The parcel of notices says BONFIRE NIGHT.
lines.text: Mine's milk, no sugar. If you're passing the caff later.
No. Just if you're there. Tell me what happens, even if you forget the tea.

lines.context: She closes her phone but keeps one finger between two pages of a drawing. A corner of the paper is covered in crossed-out lettering.
lines.text: You made it back. How was it?
Did Val call you love? She calls the card machine love when it works.
Oh, I like that. Hang on. Let me draw it before I forget.

lines.context: Her phone lights up: Val has put her down for the whole Bonfire Night evening. Nadia turns it face down, then rubs a hole through an eraser mark on her drawing.

lines.text: Wait. Sorry. I'm not fine. I don't know why I said that.
Please don't answer for me. I just want a minute to work out what I want.
Listen first. My portfolio's due, and apparently I'm on cups all evening.
I meant the signs. I thought you'd like designing them.

lines.context: She puts three small rectangles beside her portfolio. Val looks at the rectangles, then at the shift she wrote on her phone.
lines.text: Three signs I can finish. A whole evening I can't.
Three signs. I'll pay you for those. The cups are my problem.
Then yes. And my name on the bottom.
Not tonight, Val. I need to finish my own work.
All right. The old signs will do. Show me the portfolio when it's finished?
Go and see somewhere I haven't been this week. Bring me one small detail.
Three signs, delivered and paid for. Look, she even signed them.
Found last year's signs in the cupboard. Nadia's finished her own drawing.

lines.context: He moves a little mark away from the fireworks on the map. A message from his niece says she wants to see the colours, but the bangs hurt her ears.

lines.text: Further than that. Let's ask her rather than guess.
She does want to come. She just doesn't want to stand there.
She's chosen the path at the back. We can leave whenever she wants.

lines.context: Her drawing has Val with six arms and herself with two pencils. You are in it too, but the space beside you is still empty.
lines.text: What shall I put beside you?
Questions are useful. You notice things. That's a thing.
I'll leave room. People are allowed to be unfinished.

lines.context: Val starts to hand you a parcel, catches herself, and puts it down. Nadia notices and grins.
lines.text: Will you come for the lights? If you want.
Meet us by the path, then. We'll have a clear way out.
Come here when you're ready. No shift attached.

lines.context: The map's quieter path leads left, away from the gathering. Nadia points at the arrow sign and a clear spot beside Val.

lines.text: That's it. People can see it before they have to choose.
I'll take it. You find yourself a good spot.

lines.context: She waits with two cups instead of pouring your usual. The sign points away from the noisier gathering.

lines.text: Tea. Nothing added yet. Milk and sugar are separate.
All right. They'll be here if you change your mind.
We're heading to the back, as planned. Ready?
We'll walk over together. You can move back whenever you like.
One more thing. This copy's yours.
Estamos preparando la ofrenda de la familia.

lines.context: Lucía holds flowers across both sides of her drawing. Tomás sets down a blue cup with a crooked handle, traces its shape with one finger and taps an open space beside a photograph. Rocío follows his hand.
lines.text: Quiero dejar espacio para esa taza.
Esta. La usaba todos los días.
Las flores sí, pero sin tapar la taza.

lines.context: Lucía rubs out a small patch of flowers in her drawing. She holds the pencil over two possible places for the cup. Tomás is still standing right here.

lines.text: Ahí se esconde. Junto a la foto, mejor.
Sí, junto a la foto. Gracias.
Cempasúchil. En La Merced hay manojos de varios tamaños.
¿Te grabo contando lo de la foto?

lines.context: Lucía lifts her phone. Tomás shakes his head and turns the photograph towards himself. Rocío puts her own phone down. Lucía has not started recording.

lines.text: Ni corto ni largo. Sin grabar, por favor.
Sí. La taza salió chueca, como debe ser.
Las flores, si quieres. La historia de la foto, no.
Una vez quemó la cena. Dijo que el humo era parte de la receta.

lines.context: Tomás points to the photograph, mimes a pan filling with smoke and laughs. Lucía laughs too, then looks unsure. A moment later Tomás grows quiet with his hand around the cup.

lines.text: Me da risa. Y la extraño.
Así la recuerdo. También me hace reír.

lines.context: Lucía frames an empty space beside the table with her fingers. Tomás moves out of that space and shakes his head. Rocío waits to see whether you want to stand beside her.

lines.text: Aquí, si quieres. Tomás se queda fuera de la foto.

lines.context: She has signed the drawing and left room for you. You show the blank name spaces in your notebook. She points to your head as if something has slipped out, then waits.

lines.text: Ah. No es que lo olvidaste.
Sí te reconozco. El cuaderno ayuda.

lines.context: The photograph and blue cup are on the table. Rocío points to the clear left side for the last stems. She offers you the small bundle, leaving you time to answer.
lines.text: ¿Me ayudas con estas flores? Aquí, sin tapar la taza.
Ahí está. Todavía se ve la taza.

lines.context: Lucía's pencil pauses at the crooked handle. She draws a neat straight version in the margin and compares it to the actual cup.

lines.text: Se ve bonita. Pero ya no parece su taza.
Así. Ahora sí es esa taza.
¿Les conté cómo intentó pegarle el asa?
Esta copia es para ti. Para que te acuerdes.

lines.context: On the left tray: a scratched green brooch with a loose clasp. On the right: a shiny blue replacement. Alina matches the green brooch to a photograph in her wallet, then turns it over and shows Viktor the loose pin.
He draws a pin-backed badge and marks Izmaylovo on your map. Pavel reaches for a price tag; Viktor moves it aside and offers you a pencil instead.
lines.text: В Измайлово посмотрите. Покупать не обязательно.

lines.context: Viktor turns your drawing over to the side that was empty. His pencil waits by the little clasp.
Pavel begins showing her photograph around. Alina closes the wallet and puts a hand on it. Her other hand stays beside the brooch; she has not taken that away.

lines.text: Я не хочу об этом говорить.
Что брошь можно починить. Этого достаточно.
Извини. Не надо было рассказывать за тебя.
Такой пас! Ворота пустые, а он мимо!

lines.context: The man who barely spoke over the loose pin is now drawing a football pitch with both hands. He stops when he sees you watching his mouth instead of his imaginary goal.

lines.text: Ну и как бы вы сыграли?

lines.context: He has two working fastenings: the old narrow clasp with a reinforcing loop, and a wider replacement. The scratched face can stay with either. Alina flexes her fingers before reaching for them.

lines.text: Новая удобнее. А старую сохраним в коробке.
С петлёй попробуем. Так я справляюсь.

lines.context: Alina opens and closes the repaired clasp, then holds the brooch towards you. The photograph stays in her pocket.

lines.text: Брошь можно посмотреть. Фотографию не надо.
Сложная работа. Начинать надо с маленького.
На Масленицу приходите на блины. Вместе посидим.

lines.context: Pavel draws a stack of pancakes and adds you beside the others. Viktor closes the tool box before pointing to the gathering.

lines.text: С Масленицей! Блины со сметаной или с вареньем?

lines.context: The left plate has plain pancakes and a separate bowl of sour cream. The right has pancakes with a red fruit filling. Alina opens one so you can see inside. The tools are put away for their small Maslenitsa gathering.

lines.text: С вареньем. Мне тоже так нравится.
Новая застёжка работает. Старая дома, в коробке.
Петля держится. Вот здесь вы помогли.

lines.context: Alina takes the photograph out herself this time. She places it facing the people at the table and waits for their attention.

lines.text: Бабушка эту брошь всегда прикалывала криво.

lines.context: Asha's list, Yusuf's parcel and Omkar's open phone all arrive in the conversation together. Omkar sees your pencil stop. He raises one finger and puts the screwdriver down.
Her welcome sign stands in Yusuf's delivery route. He holds the parcel in front of him and stops beside it. Asha points to the sign, then to an empty patch beside the shop.

lines.text: बोर्ड दिखना चाहिए। दीवार के पास?
चोर बाज़ार में देखिए। खरीदना ज़रूरी नहीं।

lines.context: Yusuf traces Omkar's delivery gap. Asha taps a blank space for the meeting time. There are words on the draft notice, but you cannot tell which neighbours can read them.

lines.text: नाम से कैसे पता चलेगा? पूछ लेते हैं।
आप किस भाषा में पढ़ते हैं?
मैं कुर्सियाँ लगा दूँगा। पूजा में नहीं बैठूँगा।

lines.context: Yusuf points to the chairs, then gently shakes his head towards the ritual area. Asha nods and gives him the seating sketch. She keeps his place at the gathering.

lines.text: मैं यहीं हूँ। बस पूजा में नहीं।

lines.context: Asha has asked for a seat near enough to hear, outside the delivery gap. She tries the position on the right with her own feet before marking it. The chair waits on the left.

lines.text: यहाँ से सुनाई देता है। धन्यवाद।
आज का काम ख़त्म। अब मेरा स्केच।

lines.context: The gathering is ready. Omkar points out where visitors can watch and where people joining the ritual are sitting. Yusuf waits near the entrance with the route drawing.

lines.text: यहाँ बैठिए। कुछ पूछना हो तो पूछिए।

lines.context: Asha offers a small portion and holds the spoon still. Yusuf shakes his head, thanks her and carries on talking. She does not fill his plate.

lines.text: मेरे डिज़ाइन से अलग है। अच्छा है।

lines.context: You raise your map. Odile lowers its edge with a finger, looks at your face, and waits. Inès waves with her free hand while finishing a call. Odile waves back.

lines.text: Le quatorze juillet, on mange ensemble. Tu viens ?

lines.context: Marcel points to the plates on the plan, then taps his wrist. Odile writes 19:00. Inès writes 21:00 and draws a music note. Marcel yawns and shakes his head.

lines.text: À vingt et une heures, je dors !
On mange à dix-neuf heures. La musique après.
D'accord. Je vous rejoins après mon travail.

lines.context: She taps the spare chair, then an empty patch beside the table. Marcel shifts his basket to one side, ready to help if needed.
lines.text: Cette chaise, là, s'il vous plaît ?
Du pain. À Belleville, vous en trouverez aussi.

lines.context: She taps the loaf on your map and looks up, leaving room for your answer.
Inès starts to smile, then checks her phone again. Her thumb stays over the screen. Odile has stopped writing.
lines.text: Ça va. Enfin… j'attends un appel.
Mon frère est à l'hôpital. J'attends de ses nouvelles.

lines.context: Marcel lifts the bread basket. He taps the drawn plates on the plan one by one, then holds his pencil above the unfinished list of names.
lines.text: Du pain pour combien de personnes ?
Pas le prix. Combien de personnes ?
Douze pour le moment. Je garde du pain en réserve.

lines.context: Beside her brother's name, Inès draws a question mark. Odile has a spare plate ready. Inès leaves the mark exactly as it is.
lines.text: Mon frère ? Peut-être. On ne sait pas encore.
Je n'ai pas promis. Ça dépend de lui.

lines.context: She sets a plate beside the question mark. Marcel brings an empty food box too. Either can wait until her brother decides.

lines.text: Au fait, tu peux me tutoyer.

lines.context: She points to you, then the place beside them. The word TU is still written next to her name. Odile's different word has not been crossed out.

lines.text: Avec moi ? Tu peux dire : avec toi.

lines.context: Odile has drawn an extra plate on the plan. Her pencil waits over the line beneath it. She points at herself, says Odile, then looks at you.

lines.text: Revenez pour le repas. Vous connaissez le chemin.

lines.context: Inès puts her phone down and points to her brother's question mark. She turns the page to tomorrow. Marcel waits beside the spare bread.
lines.text: Il reste chez lui ce soir. Peut-être demain.
Peut-être, ce n'est pas une promesse.
La boîte est prête. Il sera content.
Je lui prépare une boîte maintenant.

lines.context: He points from the basket to the place beside Inès. The word from the first day returns with the same smell.
You have been showing Odile how your journey began. She taps the drawing of the falling light, then traces back to its first line. Her other hand rests over her bread plate.

lines.text: Non, votre histoire. Encore une fois.
Vous reviendrez. On gardera une place.

lines.context: Haru admires the tall, narrow cup on the left. Mr Mori opens and closes his fingers, then tries the broad handle of the cup on the right. Setsuko leaves the price cards face down.
lines.text: 持ちやすいのはどっちですか？
どうぞ。持ってみてください。
きれいですね。でも、私にはこっち。
はい。これは持ちやすいです。

lines.context: Haru lifts the wrapping paper. Mr Mori reaches into his bag and brings out a padded pouch. His answer sounds reassuring. Haru waits with the paper still open.

lines.text: ああ、紙はいらないです。袋があります。
いいえ。この袋に入れます。
七夕の短冊です。まだ書かなくてもいいですよ。
みんなに読んでほしいな。

lines.context: Haru lays a yellow wish strip flat with the writing showing. Mr Mori folds his pink strip twice and keeps one hand on the fold. Haru reaches towards it, then stops.

lines.text: それは読まないでください。
分かりました。折ったままにします。
約束の時間は過ぎています。いつ届きますか？

lines.context: A delivery is late. Setsuko speaks firmly into her phone and writes down the new time. Haru notices you looking from the patient cup demonstration to the irritated phone call.

lines.text: 待つのは構わない。でも、連絡は欲しいですね。
ここに結んでもいいですか？

lines.context: Mr Mori lifts his folded strip towards the high branch, then lowers his arm. He looks at a lower shoot. Haru has heard the familiar first word and is already reaching upwards.
lines.text: 大丈夫……でも、もう少し低いところはありますか？
そこは手が届きません。
この高さでどうですか？
はい。ここなら自分でできます。

lines.context: Setsuko sets a pen beside your blank strip. She waits while you look between the broken ship in your notebook and the people around the bamboo.
lines.text: 何か書きますか？絵でもいいですよ。
まだ決まらなくても大丈夫。

lines.context: Haru holds a loose string beside your strip and points to the low branch. Your notebook is still open. Haru waits for your answer before taking either.

lines.text: 分かりました。手帳にしまっておきましょう。

lines.context: Haru offers the open yellow strip. Mr Mori's pink strip is still folded. Nobody has changed his answer by hanging it in a public place.
lines.text: どれを読みましょうか？
自分の店を開きたいです。
Nee! Pfand. Das ist Geld, Mensch.
Flasche, jeden Tag. Das ist Arbeit.
Neun Jahre hier. Und immer noch nicht von hier.
Vierzig Jahre hier. Die Bahn? Nicht mehr.
Grüezi, chumm ine, mir fahred grad.
Alli schriibed Hochdütsch, keine redt so.
Not seen you before, have I?
Sorry, you alright? I'm afraid I can't let you through without a pass.
Nobody in this building knows my name.
You lost, love? Nineteen years I've done this floor.
They don't see me. Not rude. Just don't.
You safe? Bus ain't come innit.
Good afternoon. Was there something particular?
You looking for something or just looking?
This whole street used to be us.
Yeah, no, you can wait there.
Oiga, usted no es de aqui.
Arre boss, kya chahiye, tell me.
Ben buralıyım. Sokak değişti. Ben değil.
Aqui hay que decir como lo sabes.
Yeah nah you're right, no worries.
Born here. Cabra. Forty minutes that way.
Senta aqui. Deixa eu ver. Relaxa.
Voce ta fugindo de mim? Chega mais.
Junho, fogueira, milho, danca. Voce vem.
Sali. Wottsch öppis? Entschuldigung. Möchten Sie etwas kaufen?
Das isch Hochdütsch. So schriibt me, so redt me nöd.
Sächsilüüte. Ross, Zünft, Füür, alli. Chumm au, gell?
Du bist imma hier. Samstag. Wiesn.
Voila. Ce n est pas l accent.
Bappa aa rahe hain. Aana, bhai.
Mande? Ay, joven. Que le damos?
Was machen Sie hier? Das ist mein Zimmer!
Ach so. Entschuldigung. Letzte Woche war das meins.
Sorry, you alright? It's just the recycling goes Tuesday.
Oi! Tudo bem? Chega aqui, relaxa.
Sunntig, gell. So macht me das nöd.
Abi! Buyur, buyur. Bir çay iç.
Arre bhai, mandal ke liye. Thoda sa.
Ara, chotto ne. Tabearuki wa chotto...
Guten Morgen! Kann ich Ihnen helfen?
Ich habe frisches und gutes Brot.
Guten Morgen! Wie geht es Ihnen?
Ich habe auch heute frisches Brot.
Sie kommen jeden Morgen! Ich bin Lukas.
Das Brot ist sehr frisch heute. Möchten Sie?
Schöner Morgen! Kalt in der Nacht, oder?
Ich kann Ihnen das gute Brot empfehlen.
Sie sind nicht von hier, oder?
Zimmer drei null vier. Dritter Stock!

berlin_ercan.role: fifty-nine. Came at nine, four years after his father did. Mends bicycles in an arch under the U1 on Skalitzer Strasse and has not heard a train go over since about 1974.

berlin_hartmut.role: sixty-eight. Born in the back building, watched the street change twice. Walks the bins by the playground for Pfand and is not embarrassed about it.

berlin_ilka.name: Ilka
berlin_ilka.role: thirty-one. Nine years here, from Stuttgart, and still called die Wessi by men on benches. Speaks the German the alien has actually been learning, which is its own kind of foreign.

berlin_sibel.name: Sibel
berlin_sibel.role: twenty-six. Born on this street; her grandfather came in 1971. On the till at the Maybachufer market stall, Tuesdays and Fridays, and changes language mid-sentence without hearing herself do it.

bins_woman.name: Woman from number nine
bins_woman.role: number nine, and she has waited a week to say it

bonjour_man.name: The man behind the counter
bonjour_man.role: behind the counter, correcting something once

cay_man.name: The shop two doors down
cay_man.role: two doors down, holding a glass you did not order

dakar_awa.name: Awa
dakar_awa.role: wax cloth, six bolts deep. Thirty-six. Will out-greet anybody.

dakar_ousmane.name: Ousmane
dakar_ousmane.role: tailor, two doors down from the mosque. Fifty-two. Never rushed.

eating_woman.name: The woman from the shop
eating_woman.role: saw you walking and eating, and came after you

flower_woman.name: A woman with both arms full
flower_woman.role: both arms full, and now so are yours

hanoi_duc.name: Duc
hanoi_duc.role: xe om rider under the bridge. Twenty-four. Corrects you for free.

hanoi_hien.name: Hien
hanoi_hien.role: sells bun on a plastic stool. Thirty-eight. Endlessly patient about tone.

hanoi_lan.name: Lan
hanoi_lan.role: sells tea from a cart by the metro stairs. Twenty-nine. Repeats you back.

hold_man.name: A man with a broken strap
hold_man.role: a broken strap and no spare hand

honolulu_kimo.name: Kimo
honolulu_kimo.role: keeps two boards and lends one of them out. Has never charged anybody and does not intend to start.

honolulu_lani.name: Lani
honolulu_lani.role: strings leis on a needle the length of her forearm without looking down. Sells to people who are giving them to somebody.

istanbul_altan.name: Altan
istanbul_altan.role: second-hand books in a passage off İstiklal. Sixty-three. Was a translator.

istanbul_bulent.name: Bülent
istanbul_bulent.role: sixty-three. Ship chandler in Persembe Pazari - rope, brass, anchor chain. Has never once let anybody pay for the tea.

istanbul_emre.name: Emre
istanbul_emre.role: nine years old, in the lane every afternoon. The best language teacher in the game and does not know it — he points at a thing, says its name, and waits for you to say it back.

istanbul_meryem.name: Meryem
istanbul_meryem.role: Yusuf's mother, seventies. Feeds whoever is in the shop at the hour she feeds people. Never asks a question you cannot answer.

istanbul_nurhan.name: Nurhan Abla
istanbul_nurhan.role: runs the büfe, fifties. Brisk, kind, and will call you 'oğlum' before she knows your name. Kinship words are not affection here, they are the ordinary way of addressing a person.

istanbul_sevim.name: Sevim
istanbul_sevim.role: runs the fish stall by the ferry. Fifty-one. Feeds the cats first.

istanbul_yasemin.name: Yasemin
istanbul_yasemin.role: thirty-four. Runs the coffee place two streets up from the chandlers. Grew up four doors from it. Charges you properly and gives you a receipt.

jonas.name: Jonas
jonas.role: the other half, and the one who does the listening

lapaz_mauricio.name: Mauricio
lapaz_mauricio.role: cable car operator, Linea Amarilla. Thirty-nine. Asks how you know.

lapaz_remedios.name: Dona Remedios
lapaz_remedios.role: potatoes and dried maize, 16 de Julio. Sixty-four. Marks every claim.

london_aggarwal.name: Mr Aggarwal
london_aggarwal.role: newsagent, fifties. Came here at nineteen. Speaks more carefully correct English than anybody born in this postcode.

london_dot.name: Dot
london_dot.role: runs the caff. Seventy-one. Has called every customer 'love' since 1974.

london_esme.name: Esme
london_esme.role: stage door, six nights a week. Thirty-four. Has heard every excuse.

london_femi.name: Femi
london_femi.role: twenty-four. Nights on the desk in a tower lobby. Says no eleven times an hour without once using the word.

london_kai.name: Kai
london_kai.role: sixteen. Waiting for a bus that is late. Talks fast and quietly, mostly to his friends, occasionally at you.

london_marcus.name: Marcus
london_marcus.role: record shop under the arches. Fifty-eight. Been here since it was cheap.

london_trish.name: Trish
london_trish.role: fifty-two. Cleans the offices from five. Nineteen years in the building and has never met a soul who works in it.

lucia.name: Lucia
lucia.role: 44, runs the bar by the market, serves whoever speaks

lukas.name: Lukas
lukas.role: the bread man at the field market, up since four

mandal_boy.name: Boy with a receipt book
mandal_boy.role: a receipt book and forty feet of Ganpati to pay for

mexico_chuy.name: Chuy
mexico_chuy.role: juice cart on the corner. Twenty-six. Never says no to anybody either.

mexico_pilar.name: Dona Pilar
mexico_pilar.role: herbs and dried chillies, aisle four. Sixty-three. Diminutives everything.

moscow_artyom.name: Artyom
moscow_artyom.role: fixes lifts. Thirty-three. Smiles roughly twice a year.

moscow_galina.name: Galina
moscow_galina.role: kiosk by the metro. Fifty-seven. Will help you completely, unsmiling.

mumbai_farid.name: Farid
mumbai_farid.role: brass, clocks, and things off ships. Fifty-four. Sells in three at once.

mumbai_sunita.name: Sunita
mumbai_sunita.role: wholesale thread, fourth generation. Forty-seven. Corrects your grammar kindly.

neumann.name: A man in your room
neumann.role: in room 304, with a card that worked last week

neusa.name: Neusa
neusa.role: 61, the salao on the corner - thirty-one years with her hands on people

newyork_dov.name: Dov
newyork_dov.role: on the griddle since five. Knows what nine hundred people want without any of them saying a full sentence.

newyork_marisol.name: Marisol
newyork_marisol.role: runs a newsstand on a corner four thousand people an hour go past. Has answered every question this city can produce.

paris_elodie.name: Élodie
paris_elodie.role: runs the kiosk by the lawn. Has been asked for directions in nine languages today and greeted in none.

paris_karim.name: Karim
paris_karim.role: sells second-hand books off a trestle. Decides in one sentence whether you get vous or tu, and never explains which.

renate.name: Renate
renate.role: at the bus stop, as she apparently has been for a while

rome_lucia.name: Lucia
rome_lucia.role: runs the bar by the market. Forty-four. Serves whoever speaks.

rome_nando.name: Nando
rome_nando.role: third stall on the left, forty years. Fifty-nine. Talks over everyone.

saopaulo_jandira.name: Jandira
saopaulo_jandira.role: runs the shop under the red lamps. Forty-one. Stands very close.

saopaulo_wellington.name: Wellington
saopaulo_wellington.role: sound engineer, twenty-nine, touches your arm mid-sentence.

seoul_baek.name: Baek sajangnim
seoul_baek.role: lathe and press, same unit since 1979. Seventy-one. Asks your age first.

seoul_jiwon.name: Jiwon
seoul_jiwon.role: designs type upstairs from a press. Thirty-one. Drops the honorifics early.

sunntig_frau.name: A woman from the first floor
sunntig_frau.role: first floor, Seefeld, and it will take thirty seconds

sydney_jen.name: Jen
sydney_jen.role: works the ferry wharf. Uses your first name from the first sentence and shortens every word she can.

sydney_thuy.name: Thuy
sydney_thuy.role: works in one of the towers, grew up forty minutes west. Has answered the same question about where she is from since primary school.

tbilisi_nino.name: Nino
tbilisi_nino.role: sells cheese and herbs by the station. Forty-eight. Coaches you quietly.

tbilisi_zurab.name: Zurab
tbilisi_zurab.role: keeps wine in the cellar under the balcony. Sixty-six. Runs the table.

tokyo_iwata.name: Iwata-san
tokyo_iwata.role: second-hand bookshop, third generation. Sixty-two. Never refuses.

tokyo_sora.name: Sora
tokyo_sora.role: art student, nineteen, talks too much and knows it.

toronto_priya.name: Priya
toronto_priya.role: rides the same streetcar twice a day and has thanked the driver every single time.

toronto_wes.name: Wes
toronto_wes.role: third generation in the same front room. Sells what his grandfather sold plus nine things his grandfather would not recognise.

weber.name: Weber
weber.role: Frau Weber, night reception, polite at five a.m.

yusuf.name: Yusuf
yusuf.role: the shop in the han, and the glass eye above its door

zurich_frau_amsler.name: Frau Amsler
zurich_frau_amsler.role: kiosk on the corner. Sixty-eight. Speaks four languages and writes in one.

zurich_ruedi.name: Ruedi
zurich_ruedi.role: drives the 4. Forty-six. Has never once thought about how he speaks.
